key_insight: Adding ADR-based physics to TSMixer offers limited practical benefit for day-ahead solar power forecasting, with slightly faster apparent convergence but no consistent predictive gains.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale PV forecasting, a purely data-driven TSMixer baseline may avoid hybrid-model complexity without sacrificing consistent accuracy.
method: Combine the ADR physical PV efficiency model with TSMixer.
Build hybrid architectures using feature augmentation and residual learning.
Compare convergence, accuracy, geographic transferability, and data efficiency.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries, finding no consistent hybrid-model gains in test accuracy, generalization, or limited-data performance.
watch_item: The findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids for day-ahead PV forecasting and should not be generalized to all physics-informed models or forecasting settings.
paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
